title: Lung lesions with brown-pigmented atypical cells and prior melanoma: metastatic melanoma
vignette: A 65-year-old man comes to the office due to 2 months of fatigue and persistent, nonproductive cough. He has a history of coronary artery disease and myocardial infarction. Three years ago, he underwent wide local excision of a melanoma on his posterior neck. The patient has a 50-pack-year smoking history. Vital signs are within normal limits. Chest radiograph reveals multiple lung lesions and hilar lymphadenopathy. Histopathology from one of the biopsied lung lesions is shown below after staining with hematoxylin and eosin: the specimen shows pleomorphic cells with variable brown (melanin) pigment, prominent nucleoli, and binucleated cells. These histopathologic findings are most consistent with which of the following diagnoses?

clues.text: underwent wide local excision of a melanoma on his posterior neck
clues.note: A history of prior melanoma is key - melanoma can metastasize widely and recur months to years later.

clues.text: multiple lung lesions and hilar lymphadenopathy
clues.note: Multiple lung nodules with hilar adenopathy in someone with prior melanoma suggests metastatic disease.

clues.text: pleomorphic cells with variable brown (melanin) pigment, prominent nucleoli, and binucleated cells
clues.note: Malignant cells containing BROWN pigment (melanin) with atypia (pleomorphism, prominent nucleoli, binucleation) are diagnostic of MELANOMA (metastatic here).

whatMatters: Malignant, pleomorphic cells with BROWN (MELANIN) PIGMENT and prominent nucleoli in a lung biopsy - in a patient with PRIOR MELANOMA - indicate METASTATIC MELANOMA. Immunostaining (S-100, HMB-45) confirms melanocytic origin. Answer D.
strategy: Anchor on the brown (melanin) pigment within atypical cells plus a melanoma history = metastatic melanoma. Reject look-alikes by their pigment/markers: chronic heart failure (hemosiderin-laden 'heart failure cells,' not atypical melanin cells), emphysema (airspace destruction), Hodgkin lymphoma (Reed-Sternberg cells, no melanin), sarcoidosis (noncaseating granulomas), and squamous cell lung cancer (keratin, not melanin).

eliminations.label: Chronic systolic heart failure - hemosiderin, not melanin
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: pulmonary congestion with hemosiderin-laden macrophages ('heart failure cells'). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: those brown macrophages are benign (iron), whereas here the pigment is melanin within ATYPICAL (binucleated, enlarged-nuclei) cells, and hilar adenopathy isn't expected. ✅ Correct if: brown hemosiderin macrophages without atypia.

eliminations.label: Emphysema - airspace destruction
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: destruction/enlargement of alveolar airspaces (smoking-related). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: biopsy would show airspace enlargement/wall destruction, not pigmented atypical cells. ✅ Correct if: alveolar wall destruction on histology.

eliminations.label: Hodgkin lymphoma - Reed-Sternberg cells
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: lymphoma with binucleated Reed-Sternberg cells and adenopathy. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: Reed-Sternberg cells (owl-eye) sit amid an inflammatory background WITHOUT melanin pigment; the brown pigment here indicates melanoma. ✅ Correct if: Reed-Sternberg cells (CD15/CD30 positive).

eliminations.label: Sarcoidosis - noncaseating granulomas
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: systemic granulomatous disease with hilar adenopathy and reticular infiltrates. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: biopsy shows NONcaseating granulomas, not pigmented atypical cells. ✅ Correct if: noncaseating granulomas, elevated ACE/calcium.

eliminations.label: Squamous cell lung cancer - keratin, not melanin
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a smoking-related lung carcinoma with atypical cells. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: SCC shows KERATIN (pearls/keratinization), not brown melanin pigment. ✅ Correct if: keratin pearls/intercellular bridges without pigment.

reasoning: A patient with prior melanoma develops multiple lung lesions and hilar adenopathy
Biopsy shows atypical, pleomorphic cells containing brown melanin pigment with prominent nucleoli
Malignant melanin-containing cells = melanoma; here it is metastatic to the lung
mechanism: MELANOMA is a highly aggressive malignancy of melanocytes that frequently METASTASIZES EARLY via lymphatics and blood, so distant disease can appear MONTHS TO YEARS after the primary is excised (here, prior wide local excision of a neck melanoma). Metastatic melanoma commonly involves the lungs, liver, brain, and lymph nodes and can be asymptomatic for a long time. Histopathology of a metastasis shows disordered, PLEOMORPHIC malignant cells with LARGE nuclei, irregular shapes, PROMINENT NUCLEOLI, and binucleation, and - importantly - cytoplasmic BROWN PIGMENT (MELANIN granules), which points to melanocytic origin. Diagnosis is confirmed by IMMUNOSTAINING for melanocytic markers such as S-100 and HMB-45 (also SOX10, Melan-A). The distractors lack these features: heart failure cells (benign hemosiderin macrophages), emphysema (airspace destruction), Hodgkin lymphoma (Reed-Sternberg cells), sarcoidosis (noncaseating granulomas), and squamous cell carcinoma (keratin, not melanin).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Path/Derm > metastatic melanoma: early lymphatic/hematogenous spread; recurs months-years later; pigmented atypical cells (melanin), prominent nucleoli; S-100/HMB-45 positive; common mets to lung/liver/brain.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Prior melanoma + lung lesions with brown-pigmented atypical cells = metastatic melanoma.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on melanoma, melanin pigment, S-100/HMB-45, pleomorphism, or heart failure cells? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Hemosiderin (heart failure) is benign iron; Reed-Sternberg = Hodgkin; granulomas = sarcoid; keratin = SCC - none are melanin-in-atypical-cells.

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: Lung biopsy histology (stem): pleomorphic cells with BROWN (melanin) pigment, prominent nucleoli, binucleation = metastatic melanoma (confirm S-100/HMB-45).

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: brown-pigmented atypical cells + prior melanoma = metastatic melanoma; markers S-100, HMB-45.

keywords.front: Atypical cells with brown melanin pigment

keywords.back: Early, widespread (lung, liver, brain, nodes); recurs years later

firstAid.detail: Path: pigmented atypical cells; S-100/HMB-45; early widespread spread.
Onc > melanoma recurs months-years after excision.

memoryHook: Brown-pigmented ugly cells in the lung of a man who had a melanoma removed years ago = the melanoma came back (metastatic); confirm with S-100/HMB-45.
